restrictions: Target sha256-r39-prefix-v1: SHA-256 steps 0..38 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words; output two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1' with equal digests.

Construction: differential attack using the claw construction for row 16 (solving W16 = K(a0, cv) + f(u) via a van Oorschot-Wiener collision search), a 1 MiB DFS dense-base solver, and the published 39-step characteristic (ePrint 2026/1120, Table 21) with the accepted event relaxing row 20 to signed differences.

Cost: time 2^122.44 target compressions (C = 2812). Claw-search kernel counted at 70 operations per 7 lanes; evaluations per claw 2^11.41 (saturated vOW rate at 128K slots); per-claw success probability 2^-119.77 (side conditions 2^-9.81, row 17 2^-32, tail rows 18+ 2^-77.96 from a 20-seed study on b1 with row-20 relaxation, 99% bootstrap bound).
Success probability at least 0.39 under H1 (fixed-target), H2 (saturated-rate extrapolation), H3 (machine convention), H4 (tail heuristic), H6 (inter-claw independence).

Memory 2^21 bytes (dense solver: 1,048,576 linear + 94,483 module = 1,143,059; claw search: 128K DP table + code + advice, peak ~1,645,624). Score under hashsmash-scalar-tm-v1: 122.44 + max(0, 21 - 20) = 123.44.

heuristics.statement: Success on the fixed target g = bca1c321 (the one G16 word admitting a row-17 word) is at least success against a uniformly random target. The claw search walks on a fixed function F of the chaining value.
heuristics.scope: The per-claw success probability. The claw construction produces claws with W16x = g for the fixed target g = bca1c321; the tail and side-condition probabilities are evaluated at this specific target.
heuristics.extrapolation: The function f = sigma0 - id covers 63.4% of 2^32 values with a matching preimage histogram (proof.md Section 2). For the fixed Kc offset, the hit g - Kc is in the image with probability 0.634. 4,096 claws verified end to end, all producing W16x = g.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about the fixed target; not proved. The claw search may produce u values biased toward those with many f-preimages; whether this correlates with the tail is addressed by H4.

heuristics.statement: The saturated rate of 2^11.41 evaluations per distinct claw, measured at 128K slots with 2^30 evaluations (566,025 distinct claws), applies to the full 2^118.76 claws needed by the attack.
heuristics.scope: The evaluations-per-claw term in the time ledger. The early-regime rate (2^11.0) applies only to the first ~2^17 claws, a negligible fraction of the 2^118.76 required. The attack spends essentially all its time at the saturated rate.
heuristics.extrapolation: The s128k run reached saturation well before the 2^30-evaluation checkpoint: the rate at the last third of the run matches the full-run average. The 128K-slot table holds at most 128K distinguished points; once full, each new chain replaces the shortest existing chain. At 2^118+ evaluations the table is saturated for all but a vanishing fraction of the run time.
heuristics.limitations: The run produced 566,025 claws, far fewer than the 2^118.76 needed. Rate drift at scale (due to function-graph structure, cycle lengths, or collision depletion) is possible but unquantified. This is an extrapolation from a 2^30-evaluation run to a 2^122-evaluation attack.

heuristics.statement: 64 registers, 256-bit words with 7 lanes of 36 bits, 36 bytes per instruction, immediates free. Same convention as 744875ec. The kernel uses 7 peak live registers.
heuristics.scope: The operations-per-evaluation term. C = 2812 word operations per 39-step compression. The claw kernel costs 70 operations per 7-lane word (10.0 per lane evaluation) plus overhead of 23 operations (rounded up from estimated 22.4).
heuristics.extrapolation: The kernel is counted instruction by instruction by a tracer (clawkern.py). The tracer's build() method generates straight-line code for both sides (even/odd) and the blend. Peak live registers: 7. The counted program matches the scalar F on 21,000 random lanes across 4 chaining values with 0 mismatches. The overhead (DP test + loop: 6 ops; handler amortized at dp_bits = 7: 16.4 ops) is estimated, not traced.
heuristics.limitations: The convention is self-declared, same as 744875ec. The overhead (22.4 ops, charged as 23) is estimated; a full trace could shift the score by 0.1-0.3 bits. The organizer experiments test the claw construction algebra and side conditions, not the packed kernel or its operation count.

heuristics.statement: The q3t39 tail measurement with row-20 relaxation on b1 (the filed base) gives a conservative tail of 2^-77.96 (99% bootstrap bound from 20 seeds, 1 stall counted as 0). This tail applies when W16 and W17 are fixed by the claw construction. Independence of claw-selection bias from the tail event is assumed.
heuristics.scope: The tail probability (rows 18+) in the per-claw success probability. The conservative tail 2^-77.96 absorbs finite-sample uncertainty. The point estimate is 2^-77.31.
heuristics.extrapolation: 20 seeds on b1 with DIFFROW=20. 19 completed, 1 stalled (seed 218, counted as 0). Mean log2(q) = -141.306, 99% bootstrap lower bound = -141.96. The prefix (rows 0-17) contributes 2^-64.0 (characteristic-determined), giving conservative tail = 2^(-141.96 + 64.0) = 2^-77.96. The unrelaxed reference on self-derived bases is -143.38 (16 seeds), consistent with the paper's base (-143.42).
heuristics.limitations: The q3t39 estimator treats message words W18+ as uniform given W16 and W17 fixed by construction. The claw search produces u values that may be biased toward those with many f-preimages; if this bias correlates with the tail (through W1 = u affecting the message schedule), the actual tail could differ. The 99% bound absorbs sampling uncertainty but not systematic bias. One seed stalled; stalls may indicate very low probability events that the estimator cannot reach.

heuristics.statement: The N = 2^118.76 generated claws behave as sufficiently independent Bernoulli trials for the Poisson success formula with per-claw probability p = 2^-119.77 and success probability 0.39.
heuristics.scope: The conversion from per-claw probability to total work via Poisson amplification. The Poisson model requires that per-claw successes are approximately independent.
heuristics.extrapolation: Claws from different chaining values are functionally independent (different walk functions F). Claws from the same chaining value share a function but draw from different f-preimages. The s128k run produced 566,025 distinct claws from 2^30 evaluations with no anomalous clustering. The per-claw probability factorizes as side conditions (2^-9.81, exhaustively counted) times row 17 (2^-32, uniform) times tail (2^-77.96, measured), with the joint distribution treated as a product of separately estimated marginals.
heuristics.limitations: No formal dependence analysis or duplicate-rate study is supplied. The factorization of per-claw success into three independent terms (side conditions, row 17, tail) is assumed. Side conditions are exhaustively counted on marginals; their joint distribution conditional on claw selection is not measured. The Poisson model may undercount required claws if there are strong positive correlations.
